card: Allows importing public descriptors into private-key-enabled wallets when the wallet already holds the corresponding private keys. Previously, Bitcoin Core rejected public descriptors on privkey-enabled wallets, forcing users to expose and pass sensitive private keys via RPC even if the wallet already stored the master xprv. The wallet now inspects existing ScriptPubKeyMans, substituting matching master xprvs into origin-annotated xpubs and attaching matching individual keys. Closes #27336.
changed_since_previous: No functional changes to the implementation; PR was rebased following the merge of base PR #34861.
evidence: Closes issue #27336 ('Should be able to import an xpub descriptor to a privkey-enabled wallet if the wallet has the privkeys')

Description notes: 'Currently importing a descriptor to a wallet that has private keys requires the descriptor to include the private keys. This is not ideal as it means exposing private key material.'
problem: Importing a public descriptor into a wallet with private keys enabled fails unless the descriptor explicitly contains the private keys. Users are forced to export and expose sensitive private key material in RPC calls even when the wallet already possesses the required master xprv or individual keys.

risk.why: Flaws in key derivation or extended key substitution during descriptor import could cause the wallet to track addresses it cannot spend from or associate the wrong private keys with addresses, leading to loss of funds.

summary: Allows importing descriptors that omit private keys into private-key-enabled wallets when the wallet already holds those keys. During import, the wallet inspects its existing descriptor scriptpubkey managers for known private keys and master xprvs, substitutes matching origin-annotated xpubs (including participants inside musig expressions) with master keys, and supplies matching single private keys to the import keyset.
